name: Memento 2: Learning by Stateful Reflective Memory
authors: Jun Wang (sole author), UCL Centre for Artificial Intelligence, University College London
venue: arXiv preprint (cs.AI; cs.CV; cs.LG). Submitted 27 Dec 2025 (v1), last revised 29 Jan 2026 (v3); 35 pages, 4 figures. Not peer-reviewed.
reflection_type: verbal-self-critique / experience-driven reflection over episodic memory. The paper formalizes 'generalised reflection' as an iterative read-then-write loop where an LLM retrieves relevant past cases (read) and writes back evaluated outcomes (write). It is NOT a learned-critic or multi-agent-debate scheme; reflection is the LLM's ability to leverage retrieved past experience to inform future actions. The paper subsumes three reflection modes: in-context learning, feedback-driven reflection (e.g. ReAct), and internal chain-of-thought reasoning.
feedback_source: environment-reward / evaluative feedback. Each memory case stores (s, a, r, s'); the reward r := R(s,a) (or an estimated Q via Bellman/TD updates) comes from environment correctness signals or task-level assessment. The Write operation stores this evaluative feedback. In the abstract/empirical motivation, feedback derives from environment interaction (deep research, data science, software testing). No human or oracle label is required at deployment.
iteration_structure: iterative-refine / episodic continual loop. Reflection is defined as an operator T(pi)=Read(Write(pi)) forming a closed read-write learning loop, formally analogous to policy iteration: Write = policy evaluation, Read = policy improvement. Instantiated as Parzen-KL soft (entropy-regularised) policy iteration with two-time-scale (fast policy / slow memory) updates. Population/evolutionary and tree-search structures are not used.
reflection_object: action trajectory / episodic experience stored as cases. The object reflected over is the agent's episodic memory M_t = {(s_i, a_i, r_i, s'_i)} of past interaction episodes; the controllable decision object is the retrieval policy mu(c | s, M) that selects which past case to condition on. The base LLM weights are frozen; the LLM's prompt/context (the retrieved case) and the memory contents are what change. So the reflected/modified object is the prompt/context + episodic memory (a control object), not the model weights and not the reasoning chain per se.
requires_training: none (for the LLM). The framework's central claim is continual adaptation WITHOUT fine-tuning / backpropagation of LLM parameters. Learning happens through reflective memory updates (write) and retrieval (read) with a frozen LLM. The retrieval policy mu may be 'learned' via TD/soft-policy-iteration updates (a small retrieval-policy head / Q-table), but the underlying LLM kernel p_LLM is fixed or only slowly updated offline. No SFT/RL gradient updates to the LLM are required.
reward_or_critic_model: verifiable reward / environment feedback used as the evaluation signal (Write = policy evaluation produces V-hat(pi) <- Eval(tau)). The improvement signal is the Q-value over retrieved cases combined with a Parzen-window density prior; no separate trained reward model or learned critic LLM is used. The LLM itself serves as the action-generation kernel, not as a judge.
distillation_target: episodic-memory. Reflection / experience is distilled into a growing episodic case store M (multiset of (s,a,r,s') cases). Adaptation is realized through the evolution of this externalised memory plus the retrieval policy, not into model weights, a skill library, or a constitution. (The follow-up Memento-Skills extends the distillation target to a reusable skill library.)
emergent_vs_engineered: scaffold-engineered (memory + retrieval architecture), but the paper FORMALIZES the mechanism rather than proposing a new scaffold. Reflective behaviour arises from an engineered read-write episodic-memory loop wrapped around a frozen LLM (retrieval-augmented generation style), analyzed with RL theory. The paper also discusses RL-emergent internal reasoning (chain-of-thought) as one of three reflection modes it unifies, but the SRDP mechanism itself is engineered, not RL-emergent.
memory_type: long-term-episodic. Episodic memory M_t is a finite, growing multiset of cases (s, a, r, s'), explicitly modelled on the cognitive-psychology notion of episodic memory (hippocampal replay). It is the central object of the theory. (Generalizes case-based reasoning case bases and RAG external stores into a stateful episodic memory.)
memory_persistence: cross-episode and cross-task (continual / lifelong). Memory evolves M_0 -> M_1 -> ... -> M_t, accumulating across interactions and tasks to support continual general-purpose learning during deployment, blurring the train/test separation. Persistence is the mechanism by which the composite policy provably approaches optimality as coverage grows.
memory_curation_mechanism: append-only growth with retrieval-gated, density-aware access; optionally evolution. Memory grows via Write (appending experience tuples), so |M_t| increases over time. Curation/regulation is handled at read time by a Parzen-window density-aware retrieval policy with KL regularisation (balancing exploitation of high-Q cases, exploration of diverse cases, and discovery via a 'void case' c_void/c_0). The paper notes computational challenges as memory grows and points to future memory-consolidation/compression (e.g. KV-state consolidation, Bottlenecked Transformers) as the curation direction; footnote allows Q to be updated via Bellman/TD propagation across memory (a form of overwrite/value-revision).
error_localization_granularity: holistic/outcome-level (per-case, state-action-reward). Feedback enters at the granularity of an episodic case (s, a, r, s') with an outcome reward; there is no step-level, token-level, or block-level error localization. The retrieval selects a single relevant case to condition the LLM action on. This is an abstract control-theoretic treatment rather than a fine-grained error-attribution method.
intra_task_vs_inter_task: inter-task. The framework's core value is transferring experience across tasks/episodes (continual general-purpose learning, cross-task generalization via accumulated episodic memory), explicitly contrasted with within-single-task refinement. Memory coverage of the state space across tasks is what drives asymptotic optimality.
failure_recovery_vs_avoidance: avoidance-only (next-episode improvement). Reflection updates the retrieval policy and memory so future decisions improve (policy improvement across iterations); there is no mid-trajectory in-flight correction mechanism (no Agent-R-style self-rewind) and no explicit post-hoc revision of a produced answer within the formal model. Improvement manifests across successive episodes as memory grows.
task_domains: general decision-making / tool-use, framed abstractly. The theory is domain-agnostic (control over a Reflected MDP). Empirically motivated by (cited from prior work) deep research / open-ended long-horizon agentic tasks, automated data science (Kaggle / Agent K, DS-Agent), and software testing. The paper itself runs no new task experiments.
benchmarks: None run in this paper (it is a theoretical study). It references empirical results from prior work, notably Memento on GAIA and DeepResearcher, and CBR-LLM / Agent K on data-science (Kaggle) tasks. Follow-up Memento-Skills evaluates on GAIA and Humanity's Last Exam (HLE).
headline_result: Primary contribution is theoretical, not a benchmark number: formal proof that Read-Write Reflective Learning (Parzen-KL soft policy iteration over an episodic-memory-augmented 'Reflected MDP') converges, and that as episodic memory grows to densely cover the state space the composite policy provably converges to the optimal policy of the underlying MDP (Corollary 15: value gap <= 2 R_max/(1-gamma)^2 * Delta_M -> 0 as retrieval radius r_M -> 0 and miss probability delta_M -> 0). The empirical anchor it cites (not produced here) is Memento attaining top-1 on GAIA validation (87.88% Pass@3) and 79.40% on test, with case-based memory adding 4.7%-9.6% absolute on OOD tasks.
baselines: Conceptual/theoretical baselines rather than experimental: it unifies and contrasts against case-based reasoning (CBR), retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), memory-based / episodic-control RL (Model-Free Episodic Control, Neural Episodic Control), recurrent-memory RL (DRQN/LSTM), experience replay / prioritized replay (DQN), and maximum-entropy / KL-constrained RL (TRPO, MPO). No quantitative head-to-head benchmark comparison is performed in this paper.
gains_vs_baseline: Not an empirical paper, so no measured delta vs a baseline is produced here. Its theoretical 'gain' over prior memory-based RL is providing the first rigorous convergence and asymptotic-optimality guarantees for retrieval-augmented LLM agents (making such agents 'provably learnable'). Cited empirical gains (from Memento [64], not this work): case-based memory adds +4.7% to +9.6% absolute on out-of-distribution tasks; Memento outperforms the SOTA training-based method on DeepResearcher (66.6% F1 / 80.4% PM).
compute_cost_profile: Not quantified empirically. The motivating argument is sample efficiency: learning by reflective memory avoids the large-scale gradient updates / interaction trajectories required by SFT and RL, enabling adaptation 'with far fewer examples' and no backpropagation through the LLM. Inference cost is retrieval-augmented generation plus a retrieval-policy update; the paper flags that compute may become challenging as memory size grows (retrieval over a large case base), motivating future memory consolidation/compression. No token-multiplier or rollout-count figures are given.
known_limitations: Stated by the author: (1) computational challenges as the episodic memory size increases (retrieval cost / scalability over a growing case base); (2) the impact of embedding quality on retrieval/performance is not fully addressed; (3) the void-case probability mu_0(c_void) is a hyperparameter that must be tuned to control discovery; (4) results are theoretical, relying on assumptions (bounded rewards, gamma<1, stationary memory during evaluation, two-time-scale step-size conditions, and an 'LLM local consistency' assumption that p_LLM is TV-close to the optimal policy for nearby cases) that may not hold in practice; (5) no new empirical validation in this paper.
oracle_or_external_feedback_dependency: env-reward / external evaluative feedback. The Write (policy-evaluation) step requires evaluative feedback (rewards, correctness signals, task-level assessments) from environment interaction to store informative cases; convergence assumes 'writing provides informative evaluation signals.' It is not intrinsic-only self-verification, but it does NOT require ground-truth oracle labels per query at deployment - feedback is environment-driven reward. The 'LLM local consistency' assumption (p_LLM close to optimal near retrieved cases) is the key external dependency for the optimality guarantee.
self_correction_efficacy: task-dependent / provably net-positive under stated assumptions. The theory guarantees monotone policy improvement and convergence to the KL-regularised optimum (Theorem 8), with two-time-scale convergence (Theorem 10) and asymptotic optimality as memory coverage grows (Corollary 15) - i.e. net-positive given bounded rewards, informative feedback, and the LLM-local-consistency assumption. Efficacy is conditional on memory adequately covering the state space and on retrieval quality; it is a conditional/provable claim, not an unconditional empirical one.
calibration_effect: not-measured. The paper is theoretical and does not study confidence calibration or a 'reasoning tax'; entropy/KL regularisation is used for exploration-exploitation stability of the retrieval policy, not analyzed as a calibration effect.
failure_attribution_capability: n/a. This is not a failure-attribution/diagnosis method; it provides no failure-mode taxonomy, responsible-agent attribution, or step localization.
failure_mode_addressed: n/a (not a failure-analysis object). Indirectly, by formalizing exploration/discovery via the void case and density-aware retrieval, it addresses the failure of pure-exploitation memory reuse (getting stuck reusing suboptimal cases) and the local-interpolation limitation of classical episodic control, but it is not framed against MAST-style multi-agent failure modes.
dataset_or_benchmark_released: None. No new dataset, benchmark, or trace collection is released; the paper is a theoretical study (the released artifacts associated with the broader Memento line are from the empirical Memento paper / Memento-Skills, not this one).
builds_on: Memento: Fine-tuning LLM Agents without Fine-tuning LLMs (Zhou et al., 2025, arXiv:2508.16153) - the M-MDP / memory-augmented predecessor this paper formalizes; Case-Based Reasoning LLM agents (Guo et al., DS-Agent / optimizing CBR-LLMs); Agent K / Kolb-based experiential learning (Grosnit et al., 2024); episodic-control RL (Model-Free Episodic Control - Blundell et al.; Neural Episodic Control - Pritzel et al.); RL + episodic memory in humans/animals (Gershman & Daw, 2017); entropy-regularised / soft policy iteration and max-entropy RL (Geist et al.; Haarnoja et al.); KL-constrained policy updates (TRPO - Schulman et al.; MPO - Abdolmaleki et al.); two-time-scale stochastic approximation (Borkar); experience replay / prioritized replay (Mnih et al. DQN; Schaul et al.); retrieval-augmented generation (Lewis et al.); in-context learning (Brown et al., GPT-3); ReAct (Yao et al.); chain-of-thought (Wei et al.); POMDP belief-state control; EM-LLM (the author's episodic-memory LLM architecture).
extended_by_or_inspired: Memento-Skills: Let Agents Design Agents (Zhou et al., 2026, arXiv:2603.18743) - directly uses the Read-Write Reflective Learning mechanism 'introduced in Memento 2', with skills as evolving memory; reports 26.2% (GAIA) and 116.2% (HLE) relative accuracy improvements. MuSEAgent: A Multimodal Reasoning Agent with Stateful Experiences (Wang et al., 2026) - builds a stateful-experience learning paradigm, highly influenced by this work. Web2BigTable: A Bi-Level Multi-Agent LLM System for Internet-Scale Information Search and Extraction (Huang et al., 2026) - cites this work. (Semantic Scholar lists 3 citing papers as of mid-2026.)
citation_count: 3 (Semantic Scholar, retrieved 2026-06-08): citing papers are Memento-Skills, MuSEAgent, and Web2BigTable; of these 2 are flagged 'Highly Influenced'.
reasoning_model_native: Partially. The framework explicitly treats internal chain-of-thought / reasoning (o1/R1-style internal reasoning) as one of the three modes of 'generalised reflection' it unifies, and treats the reasoning LLM as a frozen kernel p_LLM. However, the contribution is orthogonal to reasoning-model internals: it adds an external episodic-memory control loop around any (reasoning or non-reasoning) frozen LLM, so it holds for but is not specific to native-reasoning models.
on_policy_distillation_link: Strong conceptual link. The paper recasts memory write/read as policy evaluation/improvement (policy iteration), and the follow-up Memento-Skills distills reflective experience into a reusable, optimizable skill library with a 'behaviour-trainable skill router' - a memory/skill-optimization analogue of on-policy distillation, but here distillation targets externalised memory/skills/prompts (read-write reflective learning) rather than student model weights. No gradient-based on-policy distillation of the LLM is performed; the analogy is RL-policy-iteration over memory, not weight distillation.
sample_efficiency: Argued (not empirically measured here) to be high: the motivation is that reflective episodic memory enables 'lower complexity learning without large-scale gradient updates,' adapting 'with far fewer examples' than SFT/RL backprop. Theoretically, fewer interactions are needed because the LLM provides local semantic generalisation and memory provides state-space coverage; the optimality bound improves as coverage (sample/memory count N_t) grows. No explicit number of trials/iterations to reach a target is reported (theoretical paper).
